question: Should the Tlon plugin adopt an unconditional 64 KiB/250 ms compatibility cutoff for successful authentication responses once representative Urbit evidence confirms it preserves supported login behavior?
rationale: The existing path deliberately drains the body for deployments whose cookie finalization depends on consumption; choosing a universal cutoff changes that compatibility contract and cannot be settled by unit-stream mocks alone.

options.title: Accept a bounded compatibility drain after proof
options.body: Fix the oversized-chunk bound and merge only after redacted live Urbit authentication evidence shows supported deployments still return the cookie within the selected budget.

options.title: Retain complete draining
options.body: Keep the current compatibility behavior and pursue a different timeout or transport-level mitigation if the fixed cutoff is not acceptable for supported deployments.

options.title: Define an explicit supported compatibility contract
options.body: Document and implement a deliberately bounded authentication-drain contract if maintainers decide older body-finalization behavior is no longer guaranteed.

recommendation.title: Accept a bounded compatibility drain after proof
recommendation.body: Fix the oversized-chunk bound and merge only after redacted live Urbit authentication evidence shows supported deployments still return the cookie within the selected budget.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history ties the original Tlon authentication behavior and subsequent Urbit hardening/refactors to this owner.
